text: Will American have a higher number of cities than Central American at turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if American's number of cities as recorded at the end of turn 90 is strictly greater than Central American's. Equal values resolve NO. The quantity is the same quantity the world report calls Cities.

text: Will at least 4 pairs of civilizations be at war at exactly turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if, as recorded at the end of turn 90, at least 4 of the ten pairs among the five civilizations are in the diplomatic state War. Exactly 4 counts.

text: Will Crimean Tatar complete the Great Wall by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Crimean Tatar completes Great Wall on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). A great wonder can be completed only once per game, so this resolves NO if another civilization completes it, or if it is not completed by the end of turn 90.

text: Will the Great Wall be completed by any civilization by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if any civilization completes Great Wall on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). Resolves NO if it has not been completed by the end of turn 90.

text: Will at least 3 cities be conquered (in total) by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if at least 3 city captures occur in total across all players on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). A capture is a city changing owner by force. Captures of cities held by barbarians count. Each capture event counts separately, so a city captured, lost and captured again counts twice. Cities that change hands when a civilization splits in a civil war are not captures. Exactly 3 counts.

text: Will Cañari capture at least 1 city by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Cañari captures at least 1 city on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). A capture is a city changing owner by force. Captures of cities held by barbarians count. Each capture event counts separately, so a city captured, lost and captured again counts twice. Cities that change hands when a civilization splits in a civil war are not captures. Exactly 1 counts.

text: Will Otomí's score be at least 82 at turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Otomí's score as recorded at the end of turn 90 is 82 or more; exactly 82 counts. This is the same quantity the world report calls Score.

text: Will Otomí found at least 1 new city by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Otomí founds at least 1 new city on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). Cities held at turn 60 and cities captured do not count. Exactly 1 counts.

text: Will Sammarinese lose at least 1 city by turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Sammarinese loses at least 1 city to capture on any turn from 61 through 90 inclusive (an event on turn 90 itself counts). Losses to any player count, including to barbarians. Each loss event counts separately, so a city lost, retaken and lost again counts twice. A city destroyed rather than captured, or lost through a civil war split, does not count. Exactly 1 counts.

text: Will Chinese's government be Republic at turn 90?
criteria: Resolves YES if Chinese's government as recorded at the end of turn 90 is Republic. A change of government completed on turn 90 counts. Anarchy counts as a form of government. Resolves NO for any other government.
